text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.07% today as oil prices climbed sharply on escalating geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf. Brent crude topped $101 a barrel for the first time since July after reports of intensifying U.S.–Iran military exchanges, including an alleged second Iranian attack on U.S. Navy ships and strikes on Saudi Arabian energy facilities. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to stronger profit margins on production and refining operations.

The stock's 3.5% gain over two weeks reflects a broader rally driven entirely by these Middle East disruptions—oil has risen from lower levels as traders price in the risk of supply interruptions from one of the world's most critical energy-producing regions. The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a third of global seaborne oil passes, remains at the center of these concerns.
